head: c0f8460e4eb0d14a62b4ae60bd94b39c2258543f
summary:
The code matches the design. App.xaml.cs parses report mode strictly: it deletes any stale report first and exits 0, 2, 3 or 70. The only lines MainWindow gains are the EndingShown event, the LastResult property and their raises and assignments; `git diff dc5d607` confirms no existing line changed. WindowReport reads only the controls' Text after Dispatcher.Yield(Loaded) and writes ASCII JSON through a .tmp file. The reader script quotes its arguments, doubles trailing backslashes and bounds the wait.

What I ran on this node:
- Build: 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Core tests: 86 passed.
- Fitness: all 10 rules hold, including the two from SL-023.
- `tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 -Case All`: all 12 cases passed against the published exe, which is newer than every source file. C-002's scan ran 1,577 ms, and CountersText after the last tick read 28,350 folders against the final 30,150, so the many-ticks shape was fed.

I read each test. Every case it runs builds the shape its matrix row names.

I also ran two paths no test reaches:
- The report folder deleted during the scan: exit 3, no file and no .tmp. This is correct.
- The window closed before the first ending: exit 0 and no file. This contradicts the contract documented in WindowReport.cs.

Three minor findings, none blocking. There is one small undeclared departure: an unparseable report path exits 2. The slice has one build attempt, so there is no loop.

findings.claim: In report mode the app can exit 0 without writing a report. This contradicts the documented contract 'Exit 0: the report was written'. I reproduced it: I launched report mode on a 30,000-folder tree and closed the window 517 ms in, before the first ending. The app exited 0 with no file at <file>, because ShutdownMode OnLastWindowClose exits with the default code. The same thing happens if an exception reaches the exit-70 handler after Shutdown(0): WPF keeps the first exit code while Discard deletes the file. A caller that trusts the exit code alone takes 'exit 0' as a report. The reader and validate still see NO REPORT, so the damage is limited to that caller.
findings.evidence: src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs:18 ('Exit 0: the report was written'); src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs:84-108, where no Closed or Exit handling exists in report mode. Reproduced on this node: `Start-Process <exe> '"<tree>" --report "<file>"'`, then CloseMainWindow() on the process I started: exit=0 fileExists=False.
findings.fix: In StartReportMode, add `Exit += (_, e) => { if (e.ApplicationExitCode == ReportWritten && !File.Exists(report)) e.ApplicationExitCode = Crashed; };`, or another code the design picks. This makes exit 0 imply that a file exists on both paths.

findings.claim: The failure at the final write is never fed by any test: WriteAsync throws, the .tmp is deleted and the handler calls Shutdown(3). Matrix row C-009's 'why' names both the startup delete and 'the final move' as having to map to exit 3 with no .tmp left. The builder's explicit startup check (a directory, or a missing parent, gives exit 3) turns both of C-009's shapes into refusals before any window opens. So the catch in App.xaml.cs:103-106 and the delete-and-rethrow in WindowReport.cs:88-92 run in no test. I checked it by hand: deleting the report's parent folder once the window appeared, during a 30,000-folder scan, gave exit 3 with no file and no .tmp. A regression here would go unnoticed.
findings.evidence: tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:350-367 (Test-C009 sends both of its runs to the startup refusal); src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs:64-65 (the pre-check); src/FsAnalyser.App/App.xaml.cs:98-106; src/FsAnalyser.App/WindowReport.cs:83-92.
findings.fix: Add a third run to Test-C009: build a C-002-sized tree and launch with `--report <case>\out\r.json`. When the process's MainWindowHandle is non-zero, delete `<case>\out`. Assert exit 3 and that neither the file nor the .tmp exists.

findings.claim: The header of .taad/fitness.yaml is now false about the file this slice appended to. It says every entry is a twin of an ArchitectureRulesTests [Fact], that xUnit is 'the authority' and 'the backstop', and that the file holds 'Five rules, eight entries'. The two SL-023 entries have no xUnit twin and are enforced only by the engine's Fitness check. `dotnet test` would stay green if MainWindow started referencing WindowReport. A reader of the header would believe otherwise.
findings.evidence: .taad/fitness.yaml:3-11 and :13-14 (the twin, authority and count claims); :143-164 (the SL-023 entries under '# settled by SL-023'); tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/ArchitectureRulesTests.cs has no fact for WindowReport.cs or MainWindow.xaml.cs.
findings.fix: Either add two [Fact]s to ArchitectureRulesTests.cs mirroring the SL-023 patterns, or amend the header: entries under a '# settled by SL-0xx' marker are Fitness-only with no xUnit twin, and drop the fixed count.

obligations.evidence: `git diff dc5d607 -- src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs` shows only added lines: the event and LastResult declarations (36-43), `LastResult = null` (124), `LastResult = result` (226) and the two EndingShown raises as the last statement of ShowOutcome (269) and ShowProblem (294). No formatting, layout or wording line was changed. Fitness reports architecture rule 2 holding. On this node, C-011 found the no-flag launch still open 5.0 s after launch, against a 0.9 s ending in report mode, and no file written. The obligation is owed to validate-slice, but its code-review half is confirmed here.

The window rendered in this code-review node, which is engine-spawned: OutcomePanel.visible was true and actualHeight 423.14 or 369.22 in every report. The validate node itself has not run, and this obligation is owed to validate-slice.
tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 Test-C001 (20 files in 4 folders, sizes in multiples of 64 KiB) passed on my run; title and both OutcomeDetail lines match the manifest.
Test-C002 (4,500 files, 30,150 folders) passed on my run with a 1,577 ms scan. CountersText after the last tick read 28,350 folders, against a final 30,150 checked from OutcomeDetail.

Test-C003 builds a junction to an outside 1 MiB file and a hardlinked 128 KiB pair. The window lines checked ('3 files and 2 folders; 1 link not followed' and '192.0 KB') would differ if the junction were followed or the pair double-counted. Passed on my run.
Test-C004 passed on my run: exit 0, title 'Could not read <root>', core.status RootUnreadable, rootError 2.

Test-C005 passes the relative root 'fsa-not-an-absolute-path'. LongPath.NormalizeRoot throws ArgumentException(root), and StartScan (MainWindow.xaml.cs:152-157, 177-178) calls ShowProblem with LastResult null. My run gave exit 0 and `"core": null`.
Test-C007 passed on my run. The unquoted Start-Process array gave exit 2 with no file and no .tmp; the same root through the reader gave Finished with root equal to the path passed.
Test-C008 passed on my run. With no root, the stale report and stale .tmp were both deleted and the run exited 2. With a root, the report was replaced by this run's and no .tmp was left.

Test-C009 passed on my run: a missing parent folder and a directory as the report path each gave exit 3, with nothing created. The write-time branch is untested; see m2. I verified it by hand: exit 3, no file, no .tmp.

Test-C010 passed on my run. The report is pure ASCII with é, 日, 本,   and – escapes, the file starts with '{' and has no byte of 0x80 or above, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads the same code points as pwsh.
Test-C011 passed on my run, and the MainWindow diff is additions only.

Test-C013 passed on my run: '<tree>\' goes through the reader, which doubles the backslash; root equals the path passed and the title reads 'Finished: <tree>'. eng/read-window.ps1:36 does the doubling.
Test-C014 passed on my run: `--report` alone, `<root> --report` and `--report <file>` each exit 2 inside a 30 s bound, and the last leaves no file. App.xaml.cs:45-49 and 77-81.

cases.evidence: WindowCases.ps1 Test-C001/New-SmallTree: 4 folders × 5 files, sizes in multiples of 64 KiB, read through eng/read-window.ps1. Checks visible, actualHeight > 0, the title and OutcomeDetail lines 1-2 against the manifest.

Test-C002: 150×200 nested folders plus 30 files each. It gates on core.elapsedMs >= 750. My run took 1,577 ms and CountersText lagged the final count (28,350 against 30,150 folders), so ticks did run before the ending. The nesting is 2 deep, which the builder declared.
Test-C003: New-Item -ItemType Junction to an outside folder holding 1 MiB, and New-Item -ItemType HardLink pairing a 128 KiB file. The expected window lines would change if either rule broke.
Test-C004: a root path that does not exist; asserts the non-Finished title, the core status and a non-null rootError.
Test-C005: a relative root reaches ShowProblem before any ScanResult (MainWindow.xaml.cs:152-157), and the report is asserted to hold `"core": null`.
Not material in the design, and no test exists. The reason still holds: a Cancelled result takes the same ShowOutcome path to the EndingShown raise at MainWindow.xaml.cs:269.
Test-C007: 'tree with space' passed as an unquoted Start-Process array (exit 2, no file, no .tmp), then through the reader (Finished).
Test-C008 writes a stale report and a stale .tmp before a no-root run, then a stale report before a real run.
Test-C009 feeds both named shapes: a missing parent and a directory path. Both are caught by the startup pre-check; the final-move failure named in the row's 'why' is not fed (m2).
Test-C010: the root name holds U+00E9, U+65E5, U+672C, U+00A0 and U+2013. The test checks the file bytes directly and reads the file with powershell.exe 5.1.
Test-C011: a positional root only; the process is still alive after max(5 s, 3× the time to the ending in report mode), and no new file appears in the case folder or the working folder.
Not material in the design, and no test exists. The handler (App.xaml.cs:84-89) is as designed: Handled, Discard, Shutdown(70). I found no outside input that reaches it.
Test-C013: '<tree>\' passed through the reader, which doubles the trailing backslash. Uses a temp folder rather than a drive root, as the design asked.
Test-C014: `--report` alone, `<root> --report` and `--report <file>`, each with a 30 s bound.

drift: An unparseable report path exits 2 without the build saying so. When Path.GetFullPath throws ArgumentException (for example `--report ""`), App.xaml.cs:53-61 exits 2. The design's exit table lists only a missing value, extra arguments or no root under 2, and puts report-path failures under 3. No test covers this branch. The build did not declare it.
